decisions.reason: 씨가 말랐겠어요 is a wipeout idiom, not “not many left”; haul is also the right word for 물량.
눈치를 살폈다 is glancing around to read the room, not watching Changsoo warily.
언제부터 needs “start worrying”; SOL drops the new-habit sting.
대답하셔야죠 is obligation; “should” weakens the poke.
“Gave me a suspicious look” is the more natural rendering of 미심쩍은 눈빛으로 쳐다봤다.
말대로 is “as he said,” not “explained.”
Private sale is the right counterpart to consignment; the em dash handles 즉 more cleanly.
이득 is profit, but 시장 경매 is a market auction, not a wholesale market.
decisions.replacement: Rare items were more profitable to sell privately. For everything else, handing them over to a government agency saved a lot of trouble. It was like the difference between a luxury auction and a market auction.

decisions.reason: Word-order swap of “once” is indistinguishable.
The cow proverb is better English, but “Apparently” is not in 마찬가지였다.
decisions.replacement: They said no part of a cow went to waste. The same was true of Minotaurs.

decisions.reason: 푹 고아 is long simmering, not a rolling boil.
Present perfect fits a choice just made in front of him.
정산 is tallying value; BASE’s “calculating the byproducts” is incomplete English.
떡고물 continues the skim/cut image from the official; “windfall” breaks the callback.
툭툭 is a sound beat; SOL invents actor, target, and a counted action.
약속한 금액은 is spoken “the amount you promised,” not formal “agreed-upon.”
SOL drops 대답했다 and turns a stiff face while answering into a face that goes rigid.
시원시원하다 is no-fuss decisiveness; “didn’t mess around” matches Taekyung’s voice.
가보처럼 간직 is “treasure it like a family heirloom”; “claim you lost it” fits the warning.
흐뭇하게 modifies the watching; SOL lets “with satisfaction” attach to staggering.
안 주면요 is the terse “And if he doesn’t?”; BASE adds “what happens.”
그 뭐냐 and 배 째라 are “well, you know” and “do your worst,” not just brazening it out.
살짝 is “a little”; SOL drops the hedge.
눈치를 살피며 주위를 두리번거린 is reading reactions and looking around, not merely glancing cautiously.
The inverted “today was the first time” is cleaner spoken English for 오늘 처음 들어 봤지만.
술배 불룩 is the beer-belly image; “drinker’s belly” reads as a calque.
혁혁한 전공 is distinguishing himself, but SOL’s “Damn” is not in 생각이 안 나네.
decisions.replacement: “He’s an A-rank Hunter who distinguished himself during the Great Cataclysm. What do people call him again? Fro… Fro… It’s suddenly slipping my mind.”

decisions.reason: 이명(異名) is the glossary epithet, not a casual nickname.
SOL drops A-rank Hunter; BASE keeps nickname instead of 이명 and weakens 큰 활약.
decisions.replacement: The same was true of Im Chunsoo. An A-rank Hunter, he was a mage who had played a major role in the Great Cataclysm, and his particular skill with ice magic had earned him the epithet Frozen.

decisions.reason: “One of the top five” is the spoken match for 다섯 손가락 안에 들다; “ranks among” is stiffer.
맨주먹 하나로 is surviving with bare fists, not “the strength of his own two fists.”
핏줄이라는 게 pivots 대단 onto bloodlines; BASE adds unsupported “power of.”
그게 무슨…… is “What do you mean…?” not the calqued “What does that…”
경쟁이 치열 is fierce competition, not a contested territory.
연결이 되나 asks whether the logic follows, not whether it “means so much.”
실력 위주의 사회 is a meritocracy.
SOL collapses 헌터로서의 능력 into “outstanding Hunter” and loses the ability/Fame/connections triad.
SOL drops 몇 년이나 (“several years”) and turns 점유 into “controlled.”
BASE keeps the 아서 cause of the lawlessness and 호락호락 as “no pushover.”
Both render 라는 말에; the wording is interchangeable.
학연·지연·혈연 are those ties, but 빼놓을 수 없는 is “leave out,” not “ignore.”
decisions.replacement: When it came to Korea, you couldn’t leave out school ties, hometown ties, or blood ties.

decisions.reason: 지역 유지라면 is an if-then contrast, not a statement that they had been a local power.
덤비면 is coming at us, not coming after us.
성격 좋아요 asks about temperament, which “good-natured” hits and “nice person” blurs.
나야 모르지 is “I wouldn’t know,” not the sharper “How would I know?”
그것만이라도 is “at least that much”; both versions drop it.
decisions.replacement: “At least tell me what you’ve heard.”

decisions.reason: A colon is the natural way to introduce the 호부견자 saying.
말은 통하는 사람인가 is “someone you can reason with,” without the extra “kind of person.”
해석해 봐 is a casual command; “Try interpreting” over-literalizes 봐.
성격이 개새끼면 is about Changsoo’s temperament; SOL drops 성격 and flattens the 호부견자 joke.
“Mellowed with age” is the set phrase for 나이 먹고 성격 죽었다.
The contraction fits this informal narrator beat.
나야 둘째치고 is setting himself aside, not “I didn’t care what happened to me.”
사고 친 거 is causing trouble; “major incident” over-specifies.
재미있다고 내기 거들었 is joining because it sounded fun.
쪽팔려서 말도 못 해 is a real prediction about Changsoo, not a hypothetical “He’d.”
박는구나 is the ongoing sting; simple past makes the nail-drive a completed act.
이색적인 is distinctive/unusual, not “striking.”
철사처럼 뻗친 is hair bristling like wire, and 보는 것만으로도 is the eyes alone.
English “What the hell is with…” takes a question mark; the thought still trails off.
SOL drops 온몸으로 겪은 and turns enduring the Cataclysm into “survived firsthand.”
돌아가고 is go back, and 당장 얘기하게 is speak now, not the expanded “say what you came to say.”
온화하다 is gentle; “mild” flattens the tone.
소문은 들었는데 is hearing a rumor; SOL drops 소문.
눈을 딱 감고 질렀다 is shutting his eyes and blurting; “steeled himself” replaces the action.
업무를 이용 is using the bank’s services, not “conducting banking business.”
감 잡았다는 듯이 is catching on, which “where this was going” captures.
담보 대출 is a secured loan, the natural banking term.
계집질 is fooling around with women, not merely chasing them.
헙 is the gulp; a bang of “!” erases the sound that the next sentence explains.
황급히 숨을 삼켰다 and 목격했기 때문 are a gulp because he saw the window freeze; SOL loses both.
파스스 is frost hissing across the glass, not a crackle.
The cleft 지배한 것은 추위와 냉기다 should keep cold and frost as the subject; BASE adds “suddenly.”
손짓 to prompt “Anything else?” is motioning to him, not gesturing at him.
다음에 뵙겠습니다 is “I’ll see you next time”; SOL adds “sir” and changes the verb.
Both drop 빠르게; 냉기 저항 기능 is a cold-resistance function.
decisions.replacement: After the branch manager fled the room, Im Chunsoo picked up the receiver. The phone had a cold-resistance function, so it transmitted the signal quickly without any problems.

decisions.reason: The receiver dies and shatters into 얼음 파편; tying “it” to the phone is cleaner than a free-floating “Ice shattered.”
내 그리 일렀는데도 is “even after I warned him,” not a pile of “all my warnings.”
The Korean splits here, but 노려보던 is a glare, not a survey.
decisions.replacement: Im Chunsoo glared coldly at the wrecked office, then his gaze stopped on one spot.

decisions.reason: K은행의…서류 뭉치 is its own fragment after the gaze stops.
들어 있을 게 분명했다 is no doubt the whereabouts are in there, not that they were “recorded.”
어느 년한테 홀랑 넘어간 is which bitch took him in; BASE censors 년.
한 장, 한 장 넘겨 가며 is turning pages; SOL keeps only the reading.
덮었을 때 is “when,” and 소리와 함께 is “with the sound,” not “as…to the sound.”
여기 데려왔습니다 includes “here.”
Keep the Korean split after 중년인, but “in the doorway” is not in the source.
decisions.replacement: An affable-looking middle-aged man stood there.

decisions.reason: 그리고 꽉 붙잡힌 한 청년 is a second fragment: the young man clutched in his grip.
왔구나 as sarcastic greeting is “is here,” not the stiffer “has arrived.”
아들의 등장에 is the son’s entrance, not “at the sight of his son.”
결코 용서의 의미는 아니었다 is simply not a gesture of forgiveness; “meant as” is extra.
손아귀 is the grasp, not the palm.
우선 맞자 is the blunt “you’re getting hit,” not the softer “let’s start with a beating.”
데려온 has no “there”; dropping it tightens the apposition.
출입 금지다 is that the place is off-limits for the next half day.
